name: Pazopanib (single agent)

source.textbook: DeVita, Hellman, and Rosenberg's Cancer: Principles & Practice of Oncology, 12th ed.

institution.provenance: ONCQIS grounded Standard Protocol (experimental, owner/device test only; not clinically activated)

biomarkers.note: Clear cell RCC (subtypes #55/#56). Pazopanib is an oral multitargeted TKI/angiogenesis inhibitor (VEGFRs, PDGFR-alpha/-beta, c-KIT); no companion biomarker is required. Non-inferior to sunitinib in the COMPARZ study. Listed as a first-line systemic option across all risk groups for clear cell RCC per Standard Guidelines (NCCN), Kidney Cancer v1.2027.

supportiveCare: Liver function tests BEFORE starting and periodically during treatment (pazopanib hepatotoxicity - grade 3 ALT/AST elevations reported).
Blood pressure monitoring and management (VEGF TKI hypertension).
Monitor for hand-foot skin reaction and fatigue.
monitoring: liver function tests (baseline and periodic - hepatotoxicity)

doseModificationRules.text: Hold and resume at a reduced dose per labeling for transaminase elevation or grade 3 or higher hypertension; obtain clinical review. Hepatotoxicity monitoring is mandatory.

drugs.name: Pazopanib
drugs.notes: Source: DeVita 12th ed., line 150905: pazopanib 800 mg once daily (the higher dose, in the PROTECT adjuvant-trial context; 800 mg once daily is the standard first-line metastatic dose), given continuously (represented as days 1 to 28 of a nominal 28-day cycle). Hepatotoxicity is a notable grade 3 toxicity (elevated ALT ~30%, AST ~21%); liver function must be monitored before and during treatment. Standard Guidelines (NCCN) Kidney Cancer v1.2027 lists pazopanib as a first-line clear cell RCC option but does not print the mg dose.
